retired.retired_reason: 2026-08-28: retired from the ACTIVE vector-PDF corpus — every real equipment schedule on this set (RTU/fan/heater/split-system/condensing-unit) lives on 2 RASTER-EMBEDDED sheets (confirmed via zero find_text hits despite a crisp-looking render — a high-DPI scan can look clean while carrying no real text at all), making it a poor fit for a corpus meant to prove/harden a VECTOR-PDF (real embedded text+geometry) pipeline. Real ground-truth keys (keys/weld-county-permit.{takeoff,reference,rowsym}.csv) and the eval scores they produced (3.8% takeoff exact, 16.7% reference, 0.0% rowsym recall) are KEPT, not deleted — this set is the intended first real member of a future OCR/raster-specific corpus, not discarded. The raw PDF stays in raw/ for that future use; it is simply no longer in the active `sets` list above. CORRECTION (same day, after independent verification): this note originally claimed the set's own remaining RTU1-x-H 'LOCAL VAV BOX SCHEDULE' gap was 'a real vector-text sub-schedule... fixed in production code' — that claim was written before the fix was actually verified and turned out to be WRONG. Direct, rigorous re-diagnosis (pdf.js operator-list inspection showing a real paintImageXObject at that exact table's bbox, plus re-rendering that bbox to confirm pixel-for-pixel) proved this table is ALSO a raster-embedded picture, not vector text — the same underlying limitation as the set's other 2 raster sheets, just a small inset on a plan-role sheet. The real fix shipped instead: `rasterScheduleNotes` (mcp/src/session.ts) now also fires on any sheet, any role, whose single largest embedded image clears a 1% area floor (`RASTER_SOLO_IMG_MIN_FRAC`, web/src/lib/rastermask.ts) — a small pasted-picture table now gets honestly named wherever it appears, not just on schedule-role sheets failing a whole-sheet threshold. weld-county-permit's own eval scores are correctly UNCHANGED by this fix (the data was never recoverable); the value is the general disclosure capability, verified against the full corpus with zero regressions.
